terms.def: Services bought by the grid operator to keep frequency and voltage stable (reserves such as FCR, aFRR, mFRR). Batteries earn a large share of their revenue here.
A market participant financially responsible for keeping its portfolio balanced each quarter-hour; it pays or receives the imbalance price for any deviation.
Standard products: base covers all hours of a period, peak covers 08:00–20:00 on working days.
An area with a single wholesale price (FR, DE-LU, BE, NL, DK1…). Germany and Luxembourg form one zone.
Actual output divided by the output at full installed capacity over the same period. A 30% wind capacity factor means turbines produced 30% of their maximum.
Combined-cycle gas turbine: the most efficient gas plant, often the marginal plant that sets the price in the middle of the merit order.
Power price minus the cost of gas and CO₂ needed to produce 1 MWh in a gas plant: the margin of a gas plant.
RTE's forecast of French consumption made the day before (J-1) and updated during the day (J). The market trades on these numbers.
Physical electricity flowing on an interconnector between two countries. It can differ from the commercial exchange because power follows the laws of physics.
Deliberately reducing wind or solar output, because of grid congestion or negative prices.
The single European auction, held at noon CET, that fixes a price and volume for each quarter-hour of the next day in every bidding zone.
German for 'dark doldrums': several days with very little wind and sun. On this site: at least 2 consecutive days with wind + solar below 5% of installed capacity.
The European associations of electricity (E) and gas (G) transmission system operators. Both run transparency platforms; ENTSO-E's needs a token, ENTSOG's does not.
ECMWF's global reanalysis of past weather since 1940, hourly at about 30 km. Used here for weather history and temperature normals.
A weather forecast run many times with slightly different starting conditions (51 members for ECMWF ENS). The spread of the members measures uncertainty.
EU Allowance: the right to emit one tonne of CO₂ in the EU Emissions Trading System. Its price adds to the cost of coal and gas plants.
The rotation speed of the synchronous grid, 50 Hz in Europe. It drops when demand exceeds supply and rises in the opposite case.
Global horizontal irradiance: total solar radiation received on a horizontal surface, in W/m². The main driver of solar output.
A measure of how cold a period is: the sum of (reference temperature − mean temperature) over the days below the reference.
The price at which the grid operator settles each BRP's deviation from its schedule. In Belgium (Elia) one single price per quarter-hour.
The maximum output of all plants of a technology, in GW.
A transmission line or cable linking two bidding zones.
Continuous trading of power for the same or next day after the day-ahead auction, up to minutes before delivery, to adjust positions as forecasts change.
Liquefied natural gas, shipped by tanker and regasified at terminals such as Dunkirk, Montoir or Wilhelmshaven.
Electricity demand on the grid (consumption), usually in GW.
Power plants ranked by marginal cost. The price is set by the most expensive plant needed to meet demand.
Market time unit: the length of one traded product. The day-ahead market moved from 60 to 15 minutes on 1 October 2025.
A price below zero: producers pay to deliver, because inflexible output exceeds what can be consumed or exported.
In Great Britain, the energy the system operator had to buy (positive) or sell (negative) to balance the system in a settlement period.
The average temperature for a given day of the year. Here: the 2016–2025 mean of the population-weighted index, smoothed over ±15 days.
An average of city temperatures weighted by population, because demand follows where people live.
Hydro plants that pump water uphill when power is cheap and turbine it when power is expensive: the largest storage technology today.
The 15-minute period that is now the basic unit of European power trading and settlement.
A reconstruction of past weather combining observations with a weather model, consistent in time and space (e.g. ERA5).
How full hydro reservoirs are, as a share of capacity. Norwegian reservoirs are a key driver of Nordic and, through exports, continental prices.
Consumption minus wind and solar output: the demand left for nuclear, hydro, thermal plants, imports and storage. Prices follow it closely.
EU regulation on wholesale energy market integrity: market-moving information such as plant outages must be published.
Hydro plants without significant storage, whose output follows the river flow.
The net deviation of all BRPs in a control area. In Belgium negative SI means the system is short and the imbalance price tends to be high.
How much electricity demand changes per °C, in GW/°C. In France about 2.4 GW per °C in winter because of electric heating.
Title Transfer Facility: the Dutch gas hub whose price is the European gas benchmark.
Transmission system operator: RTE (France), Amprion, TenneT, 50Hertz and TransnetBW (Germany), Elia (Belgium)…
